name: ESPN
description: ESPN public sports data from the anonymous site and core JSON APIs: sport/league discovery, scoreboards by date or week (schedules, live and final scores with explicit status), event summaries, teams, team records and schedules, rosters, standings, player bios with career statistics, and site search. US and international coverage as ESPN exposes it (NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, college sports, Premier League and ~219 soccer competitions incl. UEFA and FIFA tournaments).

tools.name: Event
tools.description: Read a specific game/match after finding its event_id in scoreboard or team_schedule.

options.name: event_id
options.about: ESPN event id (from scoreboard / team_schedule / search). Pattern: ^[0-9]+$.

options.name: league
options.about: ESPN league slug within the sport, e.g. nfl, college-football, eng.1, uefa.champions, fifa.world, nba, mlb, nhl (from `leagues`). Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$.

options.name: sport
options.about: ESPN sport slug, e.g. football, soccer, basketball, baseball, hockey (from `leagues` without `sport`). Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.

response.about: One event's summary from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/summary?event=`: header (status, start time, competitors, scores, records), venue, attendance, officials, team box-score statistics as ESPN labels them, scoring/key plays (NFL `scoringPlays`; soccer match details flagged scoringPlay) and the recap headline. ESPN does not validate the league path, so an event that belongs to another league is `not_found` rather than mislabeled. An unknown event_id is `not_found`.

tools.name: Leagues
tools.description: Start here to discover `sport` and `league` slugs before calling scoreboard, teams, standings or search.

options.name: sport
options.about: ESPN sport slug, e.g. football, soccer, basketball, baseball, hockey (from `leagues` without `sport`). Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.

response.about: List the sports ESPN's core API exposes (no `sport`) or every league/competition slug within one sport (`sport`), from `sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports[/{sport}/leagues]`. Slugs are the stable identifiers every other function takes as `sport`/`league`. Soccer lists ~219 competitions (eng.1, esp.1, ger.1, ita.1, fra.1, usa.1, mex.1, uefa.champions, uefa.europa, fifa.world, ...). One request; ESPN pages at 1000 so the list is complete for every sport observed. An unknown sport is `not_found`.

tools.name: Roster
tools.description: Get athlete_id values and roster details for a team; feed athlete_id to `player`.

options.name: league
options.about: ESPN league slug within the sport, e.g. nfl, college-football, eng.1, uefa.champions, fifa.world, nba, mlb, nhl (from `leagues`). Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$.

options.name: limit
options.about: Page size (default 100, max 200).

options.name: offset
options.about: Zero-based offset into the full upstream list.

options.name: sport
options.about: ESPN sport slug, e.g. football, soccer, basketball, baseball, hockey (from `leagues` without `sport`). Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.

options.name: team_id
options.about: ESPN team id. Pattern: ^[0-9]+$.

response.about: A team's current roster from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/teams/{team_id}/roster`, flattened to one player list (NFL unit groups such as offense/defense/practiceSquad become `group`) in a bounded window (`offset`/`limit`, default 100) with `next_offset`: athlete_id, names, jersey, position, age, date of birth, height/weight (raw inches/pounds and display), birthplace, citizenship (soccer), college and experience (NFL), status, injuries, headshot, player URL; plus coaches and season. An unknown team_id is `not_found`.

fields.name: group
fields.about: NFL roster unit (offense, defense, specialTeam, injuredReserveOrOut, practiceSquad, ...); null for flat rosters.

tools.name: Scoreboard
tools.description: Find schedules, live and completed scores for a league and day, and the event_id for `event`.

options.name: date
options.about: Day as YYYYMMDD. Mutually exclusive with `season`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{8}$.

options.name: groups
options.about: ESPN group id filter (college football: 80 FBS, 81 FCS; conference ids). Pattern: ^[0-9]+$.

options.name: league
options.about: ESPN league slug within the sport, e.g. nfl, college-football, eng.1, uefa.champions, fifa.world, nba, mlb, nhl (from `leagues`). Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$.

options.name: limit
options.about: limit

options.name: season
options.about: Season start year, for week-based lookups together with `seasontype` and `week`.

options.name: seasontype
options.about: 1 preseason, 2 regular season, 3 postseason (NFL / college football).

options.name: sport
options.about: ESPN sport slug, e.g. football, soccer, basketball, baseball, hockey (from `leagues` without `sport`). Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.

options.name: week
options.about: week

response.about: Events for one league on one date (`date`, YYYYMMDD, ESPN's US-Eastern day) or, for week-based leagues such as the NFL and college football, one week (`season` + `seasontype` + `week`), from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/scoreboard`. Each event carries ESPN's event_id, UTC start time, the status type (STATUS_SCHEDULED / STATUS_IN_PROGRESS / STATUS_FINAL / STATUS_FULL_TIME / STATUS_POSTPONED / ...) with a derived `category`, venue, broadcasts and both competitors with score (null before kickoff), winner flag and records. Without `date` ESPN returns its current day/week. `groups` bounds college football (80 = FBS) and `limit` caps the count (partial coverage when hit). An empty list is a legitimate day without events. An unknown league is `not_found`.

fields.name: season
fields.about: Season identity as ESPN labels it: `type` is the season-type code (NFL 1 pre, 2 regular, 3 post; soccer competitions use large codes such as 14308).

fields.name: start_time
fields.about: Event start as ESPN sends it, UTC (`2026-09-20T17:00Z`).

fields.name: status
fields.about: ESPN status type (STATUS_SCHEDULED, STATUS_IN_PROGRESS, STATUS_FINAL, STATUS_FULL_TIME, STATUS_POSTPONED, ...) plus the derived category.

response.about: ESPN site search from `site.web.api.espn.com/apis/search/v2`: results grouped by type (player, team, league, article, clips, ...) with ESPN's totals, each item with display name, subtitle, sport, default league slug, web URL and the ids decoded from ESPN's uid (`s:600~t:359` = sport 600, team 359; `s:20~l:28~a:3139477` = NFL athlete). tools.name: Standings
tools.description: Read a league table or conference/division standings for a season.

options.name: league
options.about: ESPN league slug within the sport, e.g. nfl, college-football, eng.1, uefa.champions, fifa.world, nba, mlb, nhl (from `leagues`). Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$.

options.name: level
options.about: Group depth (NFL: 3 returns divisions instead of conferences).

options.name: season
options.about: Season start year.

options.name: sport
options.about: ESPN sport slug, e.g. football, soccer, basketball, baseball, hockey (from `leagues` without `sport`). Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.

options.name: stats
options.about: Keep only these standings columns, by ESPN stat name (e.g. wins, losses, ties, points, gamesPlayed, pointDifferential, winPercent, streak, playoffSeed). Default: every column ESPN sends; a full NFL table is ~90 KB, so filter when you only need a few.

response.about: League standings from `site.api.espn.com/apis/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/standings[?season=&level=]`, flattened to tables: one per group that carries entries (a soccer league table; NFL conferences, or divisions with `level=3`), each entry with team identity, ESPN's rank note (qualification/relegation) and every standings column as ESPN names it (wins, losses, ties, points, gamesPlayed, pointDifferential, winPercent, streak, playoffSeed, ...). Includes the seasons ESPN offers. `stats` narrows the columns to the named ones. Without `season` ESPN returns the current season; a requested season ESPN answers with another year is `not_found`. An unknown league is `not_found`.

fields.name: path
fields.about: Group names from the league down to this table (e.g. ["American Football Conference", "AFC East"]).

response.about: A team's season schedule from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/teams/{team_id}/schedule[?season=]`, as a bounded window (`offset`/`limit`, default 50) over the full list with `next_offset` continuation: every event with UTC start, status (including STATUS_POSTPONED), venue, competitors and final scores.
